title: CTS The Gospel of John — Unit 11: The Spirit and the High-Priestly Prayer

blocks.en: 📖 The Gospel of John — Unit 11: The Spirit and the High-Priestly Prayer
blocks.es_reference: 📖 El Evangelio de Juan — Unidad 11: El Espíritu y la Oración Sumosacerdotal

blocks.en: Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: "I will pray the Father, and He will give you another Helper, that He may abide with you forever." — John 14:16 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: ⚡ "Y yo rogaré al Padre, y os dará otro Consolador, para que esté con vosotros para siempre." — Juan 14:16 (RVG)

blocks.en: Introduction — "I Will Not Leave You Orphans"
blocks.es_reference: Introducción — "No os dejaré huérfanos"

blocks.en: Still in the upper room, on the night before the cross, Jesus kept speaking to His troubled friends. He had told them He was going away, and their hearts were breaking; they did not understand, and grief filled the room. But His leaving would not be abandonment. "I will not leave you orphans," He promised (John 14:18), and He gave them two great gifts to prove it. The first was a Person to come and dwell with them — the Helper, the Holy Spirit. The second was a prayer, His own prayer lifting them up to the Father, the great prayer of John 17 that we call the High-Priestly Prayer. The Spirit would be God with them and in them; the prayer would hold them before the throne. Together they answer the fear of every disciple who has ever felt the Lord seem far away: you are not alone, and you are not forgotten.
blocks.es_reference: Aún en el aposento alto, la noche antes de la cruz, Jesús seguía hablando a sus amigos turbados. Les había dicho que se iba, y sus corazones se rompían; no entendían, y el dolor llenaba el cuarto. Pero su partida no sería abandono. ⚡ "No os dejaré huérfanos," prometió (Juan 14:18), y les dio dos grandes regalos para probarlo. El primero fue una Persona que vendría a morar con ellos — el Consolador, el Espíritu Santo. El segundo fue una oración, su propia oración levantándolos al Padre, la gran oración de Juan 17 que llamamos la Oración Sumosacerdotal. El Espíritu sería Dios con ellos y en ellos; la oración los sostendría ante el trono. Juntos responden al temor de todo discípulo que alguna vez ha sentido al Señor lejano: no estás solo, y no estás olvidado.

blocks.en: I. "It Is to Your Advantage That I Go Away"
blocks.es_reference: I. "Os conviene que yo me vaya"

blocks.en: The disciples could not see how His leaving could be anything but loss. Yet Jesus said something astonishing: "It is to your advantage that I go away; for if I do not go away, the Helper will not come to you; but if I depart, I will send Him to you" (John 16:7). While He walked the earth, Jesus could be in only one place at a time; by the Spirit, He would be with every believer everywhere, always. So their sorrow had a purpose they could not yet see. He compared it to a woman in labor, whose anguish is real but turns to joy when the child is born: "You will weep and mourn... you will grieve, but your grief will turn to joy" (John 16:20–22). This is the deep pattern of the life of faith — that we are often asked to trust the Father in the dark, before we are shown the reason.
blocks.es_reference: Los discípulos no podían ver cómo su partida pudiera ser otra cosa que pérdida. Sin embargo, Jesús dijo algo asombroso: ⚡ "os conviene que yo me vaya; porque si no me fuese, el Consolador no vendría a vosotros; mas si me fuere, os lo enviaré" (Juan 16:7). Mientras andaba en la tierra, Jesús podía estar en un solo lugar a la vez; por el Espíritu, estaría con cada creyente en todas partes, siempre. Así que su tristeza tenía un propósito que aún no podían ver. La comparó a una mujer de parto, cuya angustia es real pero se convierte en gozo cuando nace el niño: "Lloraréis y lamentaréis... estaréis tristes, pero vuestra tristeza se convertirá en gozo" (Juan 16:20–22). Este es el patrón hondo de la vida de fe — que a menudo se nos pide confiar en el Padre en la oscuridad, antes de que se nos muestre la razón.

blocks.en: Trusting a plan we cannot yet see. Dr. Cook has often said that after half a century of ministry he still finds much of God's working past his understanding — why God allows the wars and famines, why bad things befall good people. He has known deep loss in his own family, watching loved ones taken by a cruel disease while he himself was spared, with no answer he could give. And yet his settled confidence is this: God has a plan, and even what we cannot understand in this world we will understand in the world to come. He tells, too, of a time early in ministry when he felt sure God meant him for a large church, while a tiny, poor congregation in a cold and distant place kept calling. Reluctantly he followed what he could not explain — and it was there that God blessed the work, provided for his family, and opened the door that eventually made him a seminary professor. Looking back, the confusing road was the right one. So the Spirit comes to be our Helper precisely when the way is unclear.
blocks.es_reference: Confiar en un plan que aún no vemos. El Dr. Cook ha dicho a menudo que tras medio siglo de ministerio aún halla mucho del obrar de Dios más allá de su entendimiento — por qué Dios permite las guerras y las hambrunas, por qué les sobrevienen males a los buenos. Ha conocido pérdidas hondas en su propia familia, viendo a seres queridos llevados por una enfermedad cruel mientras él mismo fue librado, sin respuesta que pudiera dar. Y sin embargo su confianza firme es esta: Dios tiene un plan, y aun lo que no podemos entender en este mundo lo entenderemos en el mundo venidero. Cuenta también de un tiempo temprano en el ministerio cuando se sentía seguro de que Dios lo destinaba a una iglesia grande, mientras una congregación diminuta y pobre en un lugar frío y lejano seguía llamándolo. De mala gana siguió lo que no podía explicar — y fue allí donde Dios bendijo la obra, proveyó para su familia, y abrió la puerta que con el tiempo lo hizo profesor de seminario. Mirando atrás, el camino confuso era el correcto. Así que el Espíritu viene a ser nuestro Ayudador justo cuando el camino no está claro.

blocks.en: II. The Helper, the Spirit of Truth
blocks.es_reference: II. El Consolador, el Espíritu de verdad

blocks.en: The name Jesus gives the Spirit is rich: the Paraclete — the Helper, the Comforter, the Advocate, literally "one called alongside" to stand with us. And He is given not for a visit but forever: "I will pray the Father, and He will give you another Helper, that He may abide with you forever — the Spirit of truth... He dwells with you and will be in you" (John 14:16–17). Notice that "another" Helper — another of the same kind as Jesus Himself, God come close. Jesus tells us what the Spirit does. He teaches: "He will teach you all things, and bring to your remembrance all things that I said to you" (14:26). He testifies of Christ: "He will testify of Me" (15:26). He convicts: He will "convict the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment" (16:8), awakening the conscience that is dead to God. And He guides: "He will guide you into all truth... He will glorify Me" (16:13–14).
blocks.es_reference: El nombre que Jesús da al Espíritu es rico: el Paracleto — el Consolador, el Ayudador, el Abogado, literalmente "uno llamado al lado" para estar con nosotros. Y es dado no para una visita sino para siempre: ⚡ "Y yo rogaré al Padre, y os dará otro Consolador, para que esté con vosotros para siempre; el Espíritu de verdad... mora con vosotros, y estará en vosotros" (Juan 14:16–17). Note "otro" Consolador — otro de la misma clase que Jesús mismo, Dios acercado. Jesús nos dice lo que el Espíritu hace. Enseña: "él os enseñará todas las cosas, y os recordará todo lo que os he dicho" (14:26). Da testimonio de Cristo: "él dará testimonio de mí" (15:26). Convence: "convencerá al mundo de pecado, de justicia y de juicio" (16:8), despertando la conciencia que está muerta a Dios. Y guía: "él os guiará a toda verdad... él me glorificará" (16:13–14).

blocks.en: That last point is the key to knowing the Spirit's true work. The Spirit does not advertise Himself; He glorifies Christ. So a life truly filled with the Spirit will not draw attention to itself or to spectacular signs — it will point to Jesus. And this same Helper is our strength when the world turns hostile. Jesus warned that the world would hate His own as it hated Him; but the Spirit, the Advocate, empowers ordinary believers to bear bold witness even under persecution, so that the church has often grown fastest exactly where it has suffered most. The Comforter is no luxury for calm days; He is the courage of the martyr and the steady voice in the storm.
blocks.es_reference: Ese último punto es la clave para conocer la verdadera obra del Espíritu. El Espíritu no se anuncia a sí mismo; glorifica a Cristo. Así que una vida de veras llena del Espíritu no llamará la atención sobre sí misma ni sobre señales espectaculares — señalará a Jesús. Y este mismo Consolador es nuestra fuerza cuando el mundo se vuelve hostil. Jesús advirtió que el mundo odiaría a los suyos como le odió a él; pero el Espíritu, el Abogado, da poder a creyentes comunes para dar testimonio con denuedo aun bajo persecución, de modo que la iglesia a menudo ha crecido más rápido justo donde más ha sufrido. El Consolador no es un lujo para los días tranquilos; es el valor del mártir y la voz firme en la tormenta.

blocks.en: Jesus does not merely send help; He sends a Helper — a Person, God Himself, to dwell within the very people He has saved.
blocks.es_reference: Jesús no envía meramente ayuda; envía un Ayudador — una Persona, Dios mismo, para morar dentro del pueblo mismo que ha salvado.

blocks.en: This is the wonder the disciples could not yet grasp that night: the same God who had walked beside them on the roads of Galilee would now live within them. The Helper is not a force or a feeling but a divine Person who knows us, loves us, and never leaves. He prays in us when we do not know how to pray, He steadies us when our own strength fails, and He keeps quietly turning our eyes back to Christ. What Jesus had been to them on the outside, the Spirit would now be to every believer from the inside.
blocks.es_reference: Esta es la maravilla que los discípulos aún no podían captar aquella noche: el mismo Dios que había caminado junto a ellos por los caminos de Galilea ahora viviría dentro de ellos. El Consolador no es una fuerza ni un sentimiento sino una Persona divina que nos conoce, nos ama, y nunca nos deja. Ora en nosotros cuando no sabemos cómo orar, nos sostiene cuando nuestras propias fuerzas fallan, y sigue volviendo calladamente nuestros ojos a Cristo. Lo que Jesús había sido para ellos por fuera, el Espíritu lo sería ahora para cada creyente desde dentro.

blocks.en: III. Sorrow Turned to Joy, and a Plan Revealed Day by Day
blocks.es_reference: III. La tristeza convertida en gozo, y un plan revelado día a día

blocks.en: The disciples kept asking one another what Jesus meant by "a little while." We do the same. We want God to lay out the whole plan at once, plainly, the way a machine spits out an instant answer to a typed question. But God rarely answers that way. He revealed even to the disciples only what they could bear, a partial light for the next step, because He is not training slaves who obey blind orders but sons and daughters who are to grow into the very mind of Christ. "I have yet many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now" (John 16:12). We learn more by seeking His will over time than we ever would from an instant reply; the seeking itself shapes us. And through all of it the promise holds: the grief will turn to joy that no one can take away, and "whatever you ask the Father in My name He will give you" (16:23). The God who works in us "both to will and to do for His good pleasure" (Philippians 2:13) unfolds His purpose patiently, day by day.
blocks.es_reference: Los discípulos seguían preguntándose qué quería decir Jesús con "un poco." Nosotros hacemos lo mismo. Queremos que Dios despliegue todo el plan de una vez, claramente, como una máquina que arroja una respuesta instantánea a una pregunta escrita. Pero Dios rara vez responde así. Aun a los discípulos les reveló solo lo que podían soportar, una luz parcial para el siguiente paso, porque no está formando esclavos que obedecen órdenes ciegas sino hijos e hijas que han de crecer hasta la mente misma de Cristo. ⚡ "Aún tengo muchas cosas que deciros, pero ahora no las podéis sobrellevar" (Juan 16:12). Aprendemos más buscando su voluntad con el tiempo que lo que jamás aprenderíamos de una respuesta instantánea; el buscar mismo nos forma. Y a través de todo, la promesa se sostiene: la tristeza se convertirá en gozo que nadie podrá quitar, y "todo cuanto pidiereis al Padre en mi nombre, os lo dará" (16:23). El Dios que obra en nosotros "así el querer como el hacer, por su buena voluntad" (Filipenses 2:13) despliega su propósito con paciencia, día tras día.

blocks.en: IV. The High-Priestly Prayer (John 17)
blocks.es_reference: IV. La Oración Sumosacerdotal (Juan 17)

blocks.en: Then Jesus lifted His eyes to heaven and prayed — and we are allowed to listen. John 17 is rightly called the High-Priestly Prayer, for here the great High Priest intercedes for His people on the eve of His sacrifice. First He prays for Himself: "Father, the hour has come. Glorify Your Son, that Your Son also may glorify You" (17:1), and He defines for us the very heart of salvation: "This is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You have sent" (17:3). Eternal life is not first a place or a length of days; it is to know God. Then He prays for His disciples: not that the Father would take them out of the world, but keep them from the evil one, and "sanctify them by Your truth. Your word is truth" (17:17). He commits the frightened eleven to the Father's keeping.
blocks.es_reference: Entonces Jesús alzó los ojos al cielo y oró — y se nos permite escuchar. Juan 17 se llama con razón la Oración Sumosacerdotal, pues aquí el gran Sumo Sacerdote intercede por su pueblo en vísperas de su sacrificio. Primero ora por sí mismo: "Padre, la hora ha llegado; glorifica a tu Hijo, para que tu Hijo también te glorifique a ti" (17:1), y nos define el corazón mismo de la salvación: ⚡ "Y esta es la vida eterna: que te conozcan a ti, el único Dios verdadero, y a Jesucristo, a quien has enviado" (17:3). La vida eterna no es primero un lugar ni una cantidad de días; es conocer a Dios. Luego ora por sus discípulos: no que el Padre los quite del mundo, sino que los guarde del maligno, y ⚡ "Santifícalos en tu verdad; tu palabra es verdad" (17:17). Encomienda a los once atemorizados al cuidado del Padre.

blocks.en: And then He prays for us. "I do not pray for these alone, but also for those who will believe in Me through their word" (John 17:20). Every believer who has ever come to Christ through the apostles' testimony was named in that prayer on that night. And what He asks for us is oneness: "that they all may be one, as You, Father, are in Me, and I in You; that they also may be one in Us, that the world may believe that You sent Me" (17:21). The unity He prays for is not a forced uniformity or a mere organization; it is a shared life that mirrors the very oneness of the Father and the Son, and its purpose is evangelistic — so that the watching world will believe. He ends by reaching beyond this life altogether: "Father, I desire that they also whom You gave Me may be with Me where I am, that they may behold My glory" (17:24).
blocks.es_reference: Y entonces ora por nosotros. "Mas no ruego solamente por éstos, sino también por los que han de creer en mí por la palabra de ellos" (Juan 17:20). Todo creyente que alguna vez ha venido a Cristo por el testimonio de los apóstoles fue nombrado en aquella oración aquella noche. Y lo que pide por nosotros es unidad: ⚡ "para que todos sean uno; como tú, oh Padre, en mí, y yo en ti, que también ellos sean uno en nosotros; para que el mundo crea que tú me enviaste" (17:21). La unidad que pide no es una uniformidad forzada ni una mera organización; es una vida compartida que refleja la oneidad misma del Padre y el Hijo, y su propósito es evangelístico — para que el mundo que observa crea. Termina alcanzando más allá de esta vida: "Padre, aquellos que me has dado, quiero que donde yo estoy, también ellos estén conmigo, para que vean mi gloria" (17:24).

blocks.en: So put the two gifts together. Jesus did not leave His own as orphans. He sent the Helper to be with us and in us, teaching, convicting, comforting, and glorifying Christ through us; and He Himself, our great High Priest, prays for us still before the Father's throne. Whatever your confusion, whatever your sorrow, whatever the hostility of the world, the Comforter is beside you and the Son is interceding for you. You are not alone, and you are not forgotten.
blocks.es_reference: Así que una los dos regalos. Jesús no dejó a los suyos huérfanos. Envió al Consolador para estar con nosotros y en nosotros, enseñando, convenciendo, consolando, y glorificando a Cristo por medio de nosotros; y él mismo, nuestro gran Sumo Sacerdote, ora por nosotros aún ante el trono del Padre. Cualquiera que sea su confusión, cualquiera que sea su tristeza, cualquiera que sea la hostilidad del mundo, el Consolador está a su lado y el Hijo intercede por usted. No está solo, y no está olvidado.

mc.stem: In John 17, often called the High-Priestly Prayer, Jesus prays first:

options: to know the only true God and Jesus Christ whom He sent

keep them from the evil one and sanctify them in the truth, God's word

options: for all who would believe in Him through their word — including us
mc.why: John 17:20 — every later believer was named in that prayer that night.

mc.why: A shared life mirroring the oneness of Father and Son, with an evangelistic purpose.

mc.stem: The unity Jesus prays for reflects:
options: the oneness of the Father and the Son, meant so the world may believe
mc.why: It is not forced sameness but a shared life that points the world to Christ.

options: sent the Helper to be with and in us, and He Himself prays for us before the Father

sa.prompt: Explain why Jesus said it was to the disciples' advantage that He go away (John 16:7).
sa.model: The disciples could see only loss in His leaving, but Jesus said it was to their advantage that He go away, for if He did not go, the Helper would not come, but if He departed He would send the Spirit to them. While He walked the earth He could be in only one place at a time; by the Spirit He would be with every believer everywhere and always. So His departure was actually better for them, because it opened the way for the Comforter to come and dwell in them, making His presence closer than ever before.

sa.prompt: Explain the name and work of the Helper, the Spirit of truth (John 14:16-17, 26).
sa.model: Jesus called the Spirit another Helper or Comforter, the Spirit of truth, given to abide with the disciples forever and to be in them, not merely with them. The word means one called alongside to help. He teaches: He would teach them all things and bring to their remembrance all that Jesus had said, securing the apostles' faithful memory of His teaching. He is another of the same kind as Jesus, God come close. So the Helper is the abiding presence of God in the believer, teaching, reminding, and leading us in the truth of Christ.

sa.prompt: Explain how the Spirit testifies of Christ and convicts the world (John 15:26; 16:8-11).
sa.model: Jesus said the Spirit of truth would testify of Him, bearing witness to Christ rather than to Himself. He also said the Spirit would convict the world of sin, of righteousness, and of judgment, awakening the conscience that is dead to God so that people see their need of Christ. The Spirit glorifies Jesus, not Himself. So His work is to point the world to Christ, both by convicting sinners of their sin and by testifying to who Jesus is, so that they may believe and be saved.

sa.prompt: Explain that the Spirit glorifies Christ, and what that means for the believer (John 16:13-14).
sa.model: Jesus said the Spirit would guide them into all truth and would glorify Him, for the Spirit does not speak of Himself but takes what is Christ's and shows it to us. This means the Spirit does not advertise Himself or draw attention to spectacular signs; He points to Jesus. So a life truly filled with the Spirit will not exalt itself but will exalt Christ. The mark of the Spirit's work in a believer is not self-display but a heart and life that glorify Jesus and are guided by His truth.

sa.prompt: Explain Jesus' promise that their sorrow will turn to joy (John 16:20-22).
sa.model: Jesus told the disciples they would weep and mourn while the world rejoiced, but their grief would turn to joy. He compared it to a woman in labor, whose pain is real but is forgotten in the joy when her child is born. So their coming sorrow at His death had a purpose and an end. He promised, I will see you again and you will rejoice, and no one will take your joy from you. The joy is rooted in His resurrection and abiding presence, a joy the world can neither give nor take away.

sa.prompt: Explain how God reveals His plan day by day, not all at once (John 16:25-31).
sa.model: We want God to reveal His whole plan at once and plainly, like a machine giving an instant answer, but He rarely works that way. Even the disciples were given only what they could bear, a partial light for the next step. God does this because He is not training slaves who obey blind orders but sons and daughters who are to grow into the mind of Christ. We learn more by seeking His will over time than from an instant reply, for the seeking itself shapes us. So we must trust the Father day by day, even when we do not yet understand the whole plan.

sa.prompt: Explain how John 17 shows Jesus as our great High Priest praying.
sa.model: John 17 is called the High-Priestly Prayer because in it the great High Priest intercedes for His people on the eve of His sacrifice. Jesus lifts His eyes to heaven and prays first for Himself, asking the Father to glorify the Son that the Son may glorify the Father. Then He prays for His disciples, committing the frightened eleven to the Father's keeping and asking that they be sanctified in the truth. As our High Priest He stands between His people and the Father, and He still intercedes for us before the throne today.

sa.prompt: Explain Jesus' definition of eternal life and His prayer to sanctify the disciples (John 17:3, 17).
sa.model: Jesus defined eternal life as this: that they may know the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom He sent. Eternal life is not first a place or a length of days but a personal knowing of God. For His disciples He prayed not that the Father would take them out of the world but that He would keep them from the evil one and sanctify them by the truth, adding that God's word is truth. So eternal life is to know God, and the way His people are kept and made holy in a hostile world is by the truth of His word, into which the Spirit guides them.

sa.prompt: Explain that Jesus prayed for all who would believe, and the request for unity (John 17:20-23).
sa.model: Jesus said He did not pray only for the disciples present but also for all who would believe in Him through their word, so every later believer, including us, was named in that prayer that night. His great request was that they all may be one, as the Father is in the Son and the Son in the Father, that they also may be one in Them. This unity is not forced uniformity but a shared life that mirrors the oneness of the Father and the Son, and its purpose is that the world may believe that the Father sent Jesus.

sa.prompt: How do the Spirit and the High-Priestly Prayer together show that Jesus did not leave us as orphans?
sa.model: Jesus promised, I will not leave you orphans, and He proved it with two gifts. First He sent the Helper, the Spirit, to be with us and in us, teaching, convicting, comforting, and glorifying Christ through us. Second, as our great High Priest He prayed for us in John 17 and still intercedes for us before the Father. So whatever our confusion, sorrow, or the hostility of the world, the Comforter is beside us and the Son is praying for us. Together the Spirit and the prayer assure every believer that we are not alone and not forgotten.
